questions.question: Which description fits the **Goal** resource?
options: Describes the intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization care, for example, weight loss, restoring an activity of daily living, obtaining herd immunity via immunization, meeting a process improvement objective,…
A group of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one".
An assessment of the likely outcome(s) for a patient or other subject as well as the likelihood of each outcome.
A request to supply a diet, formula feeding (enteral) or oral nutritional supplement to a patient/resident.
questions.explanation: **Goal**: Describes the intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization care, for example, weight loss, restoring an activity of daily living, obtaining herd immunity via immunization, meeting a process improvement objective, etc. The other descriptions belong to **RequestGroup**, **RiskAssessment**, **NutritionOrder**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? Get the patient’s HbA1c below 7% within six months.
questions.explanation: **Goal**. An intended health outcome, often part of a CarePlan.

questions.question: You know **Goal**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “the plan to reach the goal”?
questions.explanation: **CarePlan**: the plan to reach the goal. **Goal** is for something else: Describes the intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization care, for example, weight loss, restoring an activity of daily living, obtaining herd immunity via immunization, meeting a process improvement objective,…

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **Goal** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of Goal are `lifecycleStatus` (1..1), `description` (1..1), `subject` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **Goal** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of Goal: `lifecycleStatus`. `lifecycleStatus`: proposed | planned | accepted | active | on-hold | completed | cancelled | entered-in-error | rejected. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource, so systems must understand it before using the data.
